sentences.text: Plagiophthalmosuchus was a small marine predator that fed on fish.
The genus Plagiophthalmosuchus was established in 2020 by Michela Johnson and colleagues, who moved the species gracilirostris from the genus Steneosaurus.
The jaws of Plagiophthalmosuchus were adapted to produce a relatively weak but fast bite.
The narrow snout and reduced bite force minimized water resistance for precise, rapid strikes, while its teeth were suited for gripping rather than crushing.
Plagiophthalmosuchus lived during the Early Jurassic in what is now Whitby, Yorkshire, UK, and Dudelange, Luxembourg.
Plagiophthalmosuchus lived between 184.2 and 174.7 million years ago during the Toarcian stage.
A 2024 study suggests Plagiophthalmosuchus may belong outside Teleosauroidea as one of the most basal thalattosuchians, contradicting its earlier classification within that group.
